chunks: Sulaimān ibn Dāwūd al-Minqarī narrated from Ḥammād ibn ʿĪsā, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:
In Luqmān's advice to his son: 'O my son,

travel with your sword, your sandals, your turban, your ropes, your water skin, your threads, and your awl. Take with you such medicines as you and those with you may benefit from. Be agreeable with your companions, except in disobedience to Allah, the Mighty and Glorious.'
And some of them added: 'and your horse.'

key_terms.الْأَدْوِيَةِ: medicines or remedies taken for benefit during travel
key_terms.سَافِرْ: travel; set out on a journey
key_terms.مَعْصِيَةِ: disobedience or sinful opposition to Allah's command
key_terms.وَصِيَّةِ: counsel or advice containing practical and moral instruction

ai.seo_question: What does Luqmān's advice teach about travel preparedness and conduct with companions?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves part of Luqmān's counsel to his son, emphasizing preparedness in travel through carrying essential tools, supplies, and beneficial medicine. It also teaches good companionship and cooperation with fellow travelers, while making obedience to Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ the clear limit that must not be crossed.
